extracted.intended_audience: advanced undergraduates and graduate students in analytic number theory / modular forms
extracted.subtask_description: Prove identities relating theta/Eisenstein/eta functions to arithmetic generating functions (e.g., r2, r4, partition function) by checking modular transformation laws, cusp/asymptotic behavior, and boundedness on a fundamental domain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theta function S-transformation (Theorem 1.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: For τ ∈ H and all z ∈ C, Θ(z| −1/τ) = (τ/i)^{1/2} e^{πi τ z^2} Θ(zτ | τ), where τ/i denotes the branch of the square root positive on the positive imaginary axis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This precise transformation law is proved (for real z and τ = it, t>0) via the Poisson summation formula and then extended by analytic continuation in τ and z. Use it to derive functional equations for specializations (e.g., z=0) and to compute asymptotics under τ→0 or τ→1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theta periodicity in τ (use T2 instead of T1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Θ(z|τ + 2) = Θ(z|τ) while Θ(z|τ + 1) ≠ Θ(z|τ); therefore one considers the transformations T2: τ→τ+2 and S: τ→−1/τ as the basic generators for the modular behavior of Θ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When analyzing modular invariance of Θ-related quantities, work with the subgroup generated by T2 and S. Periodicity under T2 is used repeatedly (e.g., to reduce domains and define Fourier series in q = e^{πiτ}).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dedekind eta functional equation (Prop. 1.9)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derive this by differentiating the Theta transformation (Theorem 1.6) and evaluating at a special z (z0 = 1/2 + τ/2); track zeroes and multiplicative factors carefully, and use analytic continuation. This functional equation is central to partition asymptotics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Asymptotic/cusp behavior of theta and related functions (Cor. 1.8 and others)
rubrics_metrics.description: Precise asymptotics at cusps: e.g., θ(1 − 1/τ) ∼ (τ/i)^{1/2} e^{iπτ/4} as Im(τ) → ∞; similarly, θ(τ) → 1 as Im(τ) → ∞. Analogous main-term/correction estimates are given for C(τ) and E*_2 at the cusp τ=1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To identify leading contributions near cusps, isolate the dominant terms in the Fourier/trigonometric series (typically n=0, n=−1 etc.) and bound the remaining tail (exponentially small in Im(τ)). These asymptotics are crucial for matching modular objects and for applying maximum-modulus arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Euler product for the partition generating function (Theorem 2.1)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derive formally by expanding each 1/(1−x^k) = ∑_{m≥0} x^{km} and collecting coefficient of x^n; justify convergence by bounding 1/(1−x^k) = 1 + O(x^k) for fixed |x|<1. Use this product to obtain combinatorial identities and analytic estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pentagonal number theorem (Proposition 2.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: The identity ∏_{n=1}^∞ (1 − x^n) = ∑_{k=−∞}^{∞} (−1)^k x^{k(3k+1)/2} holds (formal/analytic) and encodes cancellations between even/odd numbers of unequal parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prove via the Jacobi triple product (specializing q and z appropriately) or combinatorially. Use the theorem to derive recurrence relations for p(n) and parity/alternating-count results for partitions into unequal parts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use modular transformations of generating functions to obtain asymptotics
rubrics_metrics.description: The asymptotic behavior of partition or theta-generated sequences as the index grows is obtained by studying the modular (functional) equations of the generating function (e.g., via η(−1/τ) relation) and analyzing behavior near τ→0 or cusps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convert coefficient/asymptotic questions into studying the generating function near singular points (τ→0 or |x|→1), then use functional equations to move to a region where a Fourier expansion is controlled. This method yields sharp asymptotics for p(n).

rubrics_metrics.name: Relate counting functions to powers of θ (equations (6) and analogous)
rubrics_metrics.description: θ(τ)^2 = ∑_{n=0}^∞ r2(n) q^n (q = e^{πiτ}) and θ(τ)^4 = ∑_{n=0}^∞ r4(n) q^n; thus powers of θ are generating functions for representations as sums of squares.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derive by expanding θ as ∑_{m∈Z} q^{m^2} and grouping pairs (or quadruples) to count representations. This analytic encoding permits translating arithmetic questions into equalities of modular/analytic functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translating arithmetic formulas to analytic modular identities (Prop. 3.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: An arithmetic formula like r2(n) = 4(d1(n) − d3(n)) is equivalent to an analytic identity for θ(τ)^2 (e.g., θ(τ)^2 = 1 + 4∑_{n≥1} q^n/(1 + q^{2n})), obtained by reorganizing Fourier expansions and identifying divisor-sum coefficients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match Fourier coefficients on both sides by writing Dirichlet-type divisor sums as geometric-series manipulations (1/(1 − q^{4n}) expansions) and interpreting coefficients combinatorially as counts of divisors of specified residue classes modulo 4.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion for modular holomorphic function constancy (Theorem 3.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: If f is holomorphic on H and satisfies (i) f(τ+2)=f(τ), (ii) f(−1/τ)=f(τ), and (iii) f is bounded on H, then f is constant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof strategy: pass to the punctured unit disk by z=e^{πiτ}, remove the singularity at 0 (boundedness), map H into the fundamental domain F using T2 and S, then apply the maximum modulus principle and study behavior at cusps (τ→1) after conjugation µ(τ)=1/(1−τ). This criterion is the workhorse to show two modular objects with identical modular/cusp data differ by a constant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction to a fundamental domain via T2 and S (Lemma 3.5 / fundamental domain F)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every τ∈H can be mapped into F = {τ∈H : |Re τ| ≤ 1 and |τ| ≥ 1} by repeated application of T2: τ→τ+2 and S: τ→−1/τ; F is a fundamental domain for the group generated by T2 and S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct g in the group to maximize Im(g(τ)) and translate to ensure |Re|≤1; if |g(τ)|<1 then apply S to increase Im, contradiction. Use this algorithmic reduction to check boundedness and cusp behavior by restricting attention to F.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modular-identity proof template (compare transformations + asymptotics)
rubrics_metrics.description: To prove an identity between two modular/holomorphic objects (e.g., θ(τ)^2 = C(τ) or θ(τ)^4 = −π^{-2}E*_2(τ)), show both sides satisfy the same periodicity and S-transformation, have matching limits as Im(τ)→∞, and matching cusp asymptotics; then apply the constancy theorem to their quotient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify (a) invariance/transform law under T2 and S, (b) boundedness on fundamental domain (or known limits at cusps/infinity), and (c) nonvanishing where required (to ensure holomorphy of quotient). The quotient must then be a constant; determine its value by evaluating a limit or first Fourier coefficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and modular properties of the modified Eisenstein series E*_2 (for r4)
rubrics_metrics.description: E*_2(τ) := ∑_{m,n}' [1/(mτ + n)^2 − 1/(mτ + n)^2 with different scaling as specified] (order of summation matters); it satisfies (i) E*_2(τ+2)=E*_2(τ), (ii) E*_2(−1/τ)=−τ^2 E*_2(τ), (iii) E*_2(τ)→−π^2 as Im(τ)→∞, and (iv) controlled cusp asymptotics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct E*_2 from a (non-absolutely convergent) Eisenstein-type double sum with a careful prescribed summation order (e.g., sum over n then m). Use relations to the 'forbidden' series F and its Fourier expansion to extract Fourier coefficients (σ*_1(n)) and to derive transformation formulas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling non-absolutely convergent Eisenstein series and reverse summation (Lemma 3.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: For the forbidden Eisenstein series F (sum over m then n) and its reverse ˜F (sum over n then m), one has identities: (a) F(−1/τ)=τ^2 ˜F(τ), (b) F(τ)−˜F(τ)=2πi/τ, and (c) F(−1/τ)=τ^2 F(τ)−2πiτ. These relations follow from careful use of the eta functional equation and logarithmic differentiation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the double sums are not absolutely convergent, the order of summation changes the value by explicit correction terms; use the Dedekind eta functional equation and its log-derivative to compute those corrections and obtain precise transformation laws for E*_2 built from F.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generating-function method for solving linear recurrences (Exercises 2–3)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a linear recurrence u_n = a u_{n−1} + b u_{n−2} with given initial values, the generating function U(x) satisfies U(x)(1 − a x − b x^2) = polynomial; factor the denominator (1 − α x)(1 − β x), expand partial fractions, and extract closed-form u_n = A α^n + B β^n (distinct roots case).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use algebraic manipulation of generating functions, partial fraction decomposition, and identification of geometric-series expansions to solve recurrences. Works for distinct roots; handle repeated-root cases via generalized partial fractions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Derive partition recurrence from pentagonal theorem (Exercise 4)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equate coefficients of x^n on both sides; the right-hand side is a finite alternating sum indexed by pentagonal numbers. Use this recurrence to compute p(n) values finitely and to study parity/cancellations in p(n).

rubrics_metrics.name: Singularity analysis for partition asymptotics (Exercises 5–6)
rubrics_metrics.description: As x→1− (x real), log F(x) ∼ π^2/[6(1 − x)], and this singularity analysis yields bounds of the form p(n) ≍ exp(c n^{1/2}).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimate log F(x)=∑_{m≥1} x^m/(m(1 − x^m)) and bound by approximating sums/integrals; convert saddle/singularity information into coefficient growth bounds by choosing x=e^{−y} with y→0 and optimizing to obtain two-sided exponential-in-√n bounds for p(n).
